text: Mia looked out her big, round window.
She saw the blue sky and puffy white clouds.
But Mia felt sad.
She wanted to fly up high, past the clouds, into the stars.
Mia’s teddy bear, Ben, sat beside her.
“Why are you sad?” he asked.
“I want to go to the moon,” Mia said with a little sigh.
Ben hugged her.
“Let’s build a rocket!” Mia’s eyes lit up.
She found a cardboard box, some shiny paper, and tape.
She taped the paper on the box and drew a round window on the side.
“Our rocket has a window too!” she said.
They climbed inside.
Mia held Ben tight.
“Ready?” she asked.
“Ready!” Ben said.
Mia pushed a button on the box.
“Zoom!” she shouted.
She bounced up and down.
Ben bounced too.
They pretended to fly past the clouds, past the moon, and into the sparkly stars.
Mia looked through her cardboard window and laughed.
She wasn’t sad anymore.
She was happy, flying high with her best friend.
When they landed, Mia gave Ben a big hug.
“We went to the stars,” she said.
“And we can go again tomorrow.” Mia looked out the real window and smiled.
The sky was still there, and so was her rocket.
One morning, Mia woke up and saw her mother by the window.
“Look,” said mother, “the sun is hiding behind the clouds.” Mia looked up.
The sun was not happy.
It sat low and gray, with no warm light.
“Oh no,” said Mia.
“The sun lost its smile.” Mother gave Mia a big hug.
“Maybe we can help the sun find its smile,” she said.
Mia thought and thought.
Then she had an idea.
“Let’s make the sun laugh!” She jumped high and clapped her hands.
Mother danced and spun around.
Mia giggled and made funny faces at the sky.
The clouds wiggled.
The sun peeked out a tiny bit.
“More!” said Mia.
Mother lifted Mia up high, and Mia waved her arms wide.
“Hello, sun!
Come out and play!” Then the sun broke through the clouds with a big, golden smile.
Warm light filled the room.
Mia laughed, and mother smiled too.
“You did it,” said mother.
Mia looked at the bright sun and said, “The sun is happy again.
And I am happy too.” And the sun shone all day long, just for Mia and her mother.
Mia went outside to the garden.
The sun was warm, and the flowers were sleepy.
In the corner, Mia saw one big, red strawberry.
It sat on the ground like a tiny red ball.
Mia bent down to pick it up, but the strawberry rolled away.
"Stop!" she said.
The strawberry rolled faster.
Mia began to run.
Run, run, run across the soft grass.
The strawberry bounced under a bush.
Mia peeked under the bush.
There was a little baby bird.
The baby bird chirped and looked at the strawberry.
It wanted the strawberry, but it was too small to reach.
Mia said, "I can help you, baby bird." She reached under the bush and gently picked up the strawberry.
Then she broke it into two soft pieces.
One piece for the baby bird.
One piece for Mia.
The baby bird ate its piece and chirped, "Thank you." Mia ate her piece.
It was sweet and yummy.
Then Mia said, "Goodbye, baby bird." She smiled and walked back through the garden.
The sun was still warm, and Mia felt happy.
She had a new little friend.
Mia woke up to a funny sound.
Tap, tap, tap.
She looked out the window.
A little chicken was pecking at a big red drum.
“Hello, chicken!” said Mia.
“Why are you tapping?” The chicken clucked and pointed with its wing.
The drum had a tiny crack.
The chicken wanted to fix it, but it was too small.
Mia smiled.
“I can help!” She found some glue and a soft cloth.
The chicken held the drum steady with its feet.
Mia dabbed the glue on the crack.
Then the chicken tapped the drum again.
Tap, tap, tap!
The drum made a happy sound.
The chicken did a little dance, and Mia clapped her hands.
“Good job, chicken!” she said.
The chicken hopped onto Mia’s lap and gave her a soft peck on the cheek.
Then it tapped the drum one more time.
Tap, tap, tap!
Mia laughed.
“You are the best drumming chicken ever!” And they played together until the sun went down.
